div.span: - The client calls the instance on port 8080. The security group opens that port, plus 22 for SSH, 8001-8005 to reach a backend directly and 8404 for the stats page.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 201px; margin-left: 1311px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;

div.span: - The configured algorithm chooses web1, web2 or web3 on 127.0.0.1:8001-8003: round robin, least connections, random, weighted, source IP hash or URI hash. The frontend runs in HTTP mode, so the choice happens at layer 7, and HAProxy relays the answer back on the same connection.

div.b: Health checks decide who is UP

div.span: - Every server is probed every 2 seconds. Two good checks mark it UP, three failed checks mark it DOWN and take it out of the rotation.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 501px; margin-left: 1311px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;

display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.b: The backups answer only as a last resort

div.span: - web4 and web5 carry the backup flag, so they stay idle until all three active servers are DOWN. As soon as one active server recovers, the backups go quiet again.

div.b: The stats page runs on port 8404

div.span: - A second HAProxy frontend serves /stats, where every server shows its state, its weight and how many requests it has taken.

b.span: HAProxy is the single point of failure

div.span: - Five backends do not make the setup highly available. One HAProxy process is the only way in, and it shares the instance with every backend, so losing that process or that host takes the whole service down.
